name: Caesar cipher shift 1
idea: A fixed monoalphabetic substitution over the English alphabet using a Caesar shift of 1. Each plaintext letter is replaced by the next letter in the alphabet, with z wrapping around to a. The mapping is the same for uppercase and lowercase letters. Non-letter characters are left unchanged.
encrypt_rules: Use the following bijection: plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz -> ciphertext alphabet bcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyza. Thus a->b, b->c, c->d, d->e, e->f, f->g, g->h, h->i, i->j, j->k, k->l, l->m, m->n, n->o, o->p, p->q, q->r, r->s, s->t, t->u, u->v, v->w, w->x, x->y, y->z, z->a. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.
decrypt_rules: Use the inverse bijection: ciphertext alphabet bcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyza -> plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz. Thus b->a, c->b, d->c, e->d, f->e, g->f, h->g, i->h, j->i, k->j, l->k, m->l, n->m, o->n, p->o, q->p, r->q, s->r, t->s, u->t, v->u, w->v, x->w, y->x, z->y, a->z. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.
